previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, flank pain, and purulent drainage from his left nephrostomy tube site, consistent with cellulitis and complicated cystitis. He had a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder with ileal conduit, chronic kidney disease, and recurrent urinary infections. Initial treatment with IV meropenem was complicated by a mild rash, managed with antihistamines. Blood cultures were negative, and later urine cultures showed no growth. The infection resolved after a 7-day course of antibiotics. He was transitioned to suppressive oral fosfomycin therapy and discharged home in stable condition. A nephrostomy tube exchange was scheduled for outpatient follow-up. His chronic conditions, including pain, anxiety, and anemia, were managed throughout the stay.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man with neurogenic bladder L ureteral-conduit
stricture maintained with L PCN. L PCN fell out today.  // Replace L PCN

COMPARISON:  Prior replacement study ___

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiologist performed the
procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 7 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS:  As above
CONTRAST: 10 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  1.2 min, 2 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Tract sinogram
2. Left diagnostic antegrade nephrostogram.
3. Left 8 ___ nephrostomy replacement via existing tract.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient.The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed prone
on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol. 
The left flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Local 1% lidocaine was administered.  An initial fluoroscopic image was
obtained. The existing tube had been pulled out.  A ___ dilator was placed at
the exit site, and a tract sinogram was performed with diluted contrast.  The
image was stored on PACS.  A glidewire was advanced into the tract and coiled
in the collecting system.  The ___ dilator was advanced, wire removed, and
contrast injected to confirm position within the renal pelvis.    A new 8
___ nephrostomy catheter was flushed and advanced with its plastic
stiffener over the wire into appropriate position. The wire and stiffener were
removed and the pigtail was formed. Contrast injection confirmed appropriate
positioning. The final image was saved. The catheter was then flushed, and the
catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and sterile dressings (no suture
placed as the site was mildly inflamed).  The catheter was attached to a bag
for drainage.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Tract sinogram demonstrates a patent tract to the left kidney.
2. Left antegrade nephrostogram shows hydronephrosis and a dilated proximal
ureter.  Clear urine drained from the renal pelvis..
3. Appropriate final position of left nephrostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful left 8 ___ nephrostomy tube replacement.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Routine exchange in 3 months.
